question: Competition Act was set up in ________ replacing ________ Act.
solution:
The correct answer is __**2002; MRTP.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act of 1969** was repealed on **May 20, 2009**, when the** Competition Act of 2002 **went into effect. 
 
• The act was passed in** December 2002**, and on** January 14, 2003, **it became effective. 
 
• To implement the terms of the **Competition Act, 2002** the Indian Competition Commission (CCI) was set up on **October 14, 2003.**
 
• On **May 19, 2009, Mr. Dhanendra Kumar **was appointed as the **CCI's chairman.**
 
• There were **no laws in India** that governed or **outlawed anti-competitive agreements **prior to the passage of **the Competition Act.**
 
• In **New Delhi,** it has its **headquarters.**
 
• It has **six regional offices**, located in **Bangalore, Hyderabad, Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, and Chennai. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

** Objectives of Competition Act:-**

 
• ​The Competition Act is a piece of **legislation** whose goal is to guarantee that** consumer interests **are shielded from **anti-competitive behavior.**
 
• It supports and **sustains market competition**,** safeguards the interests of consumers, **and ensures that** other market participants** in India are free to conduct business as usual.
 
• The **three foundational pieces of competition legislation **upon which the Competition Act is built are the
 
 
• National Competition Policy,
 
• the Competition Appellate Tribunal, and
 
• the Competition Commission of India (CCI).
 
 
 
• The major reason for passing this legislation is to make sure that** market competition operates as intended** and that customers have access to a **broader variety of goods** at reasonable costs.
 
• It also strives to **prevent anti-competitive business practices** and **advance consumers' economic interests** in MERS.
